schema.title: Response List Accounts Api Accounts Get

post.description:
Register an account. A `credential` is written to the SOPS file first
(as `account-<id>`); the registry row only ever holds the reference.

The agent could not lease an account and so cannot claim: park the ready tasks
it could have taken as `awaiting_quota`. `409 account_available` if one is usable.

Start the official client's `setup-token` login for a new `anthropic`
account, or to renew `renew_account_id` (claude accounts spec 3).
Hand the sign-in page's code to the waiting client, once.

Start the official client's device-code login for a new `openai` account
(codex accounts spec 3). On success the account appears in the registry.

get.description:
Tokens and estimated cost per account, project and day over the window
ending now (cost view 3.3). Read only.

post.description:
Lease the best usable account and deliver its credential to a claimed task.

`runtime_providers` is required and states what the runtime can apply. The
caller must hold the live claim identified by `task_id` and `attempt`; only the
internal orchestrator may leave them out, for its engine (internal orchestrator
spec 3.1). One active lease per role; `409 no_account` when none is usable. A `local` lease
whose credential names no `context_tokens` carries the window the local model's
probe measured, so the harness can compact in time (local harness spec, "Harness orchestrates only").
End the agent's leases: one `role`, or all of them.

get.description:
Reported tokens per account over [from, to), bucketed in the viewer's
timezone (account usage 3.5). Buckets with no rows are measured zeros.

delete.description:
Delete an account and, if nothing else references it, its Argus-generated
credential. `confirm_name` must equal the current name; `409 account_in_use`
while a lease is active.

SOPS and SQLite cannot commit together. The secret is removed inside the SQL
transaction, so a store failure rolls the rows back; if the commit then fails
after the secret is gone, the exact prior value is written back (compensation,
best effort: if that write also fails the error names the entry, never a value).

post.description: Record `account.auth_rejected` for a held account without exhausting it.

put.description:
Replace the credential (e.g. refreshed OAuth tokens). Allowed for the agent
holding a lease on the account, or an admin. If it cannot be persisted, the
account is disabled rather than left with a token that would be lost.

An agent must also hold the live task claim named by `task_id` and `attempt`,
checked before the store write (no transaction spans the store's I/O).

post.description:
Mark a leased account exhausted and return fallback metadata only.

The caller must hold the live claim identified by `task_id` and `attempt`;
`runtime_providers` controls which fallback metadata may be returned. Obtain
any next credential through `/accounts/lease`.

get.description:
The hosts serving an OpenRouter model, with quantization, context and price,
for the routing pickers (custom accounts spec 3). Proxied; `author` and `slug`
are validated as one path segment each.

post.description:
Readiness of a custom account: `GET {base_url}/models` with its key (custom
accounts spec 3). Returns the model ids as suggestions; never the key, and
only a fixed reason, never upstream text.

Read the provider's quota now (account usage 3.3), for any account that has a
read-only source. At most once per account per 5 minutes; never refreshes the
credential. The answer carries the outcome (with a `code` when not updated) and
the figures now stored; an account with no source answers `skipped` and why.

Re-read the SOPS file after editing it by hand (`sops secrets.sops.yaml`),
then re-check every account's secret reference.

schema.title: Response List Admin Tokens Api Admin Tokens Get

post.description: Mint another admin token. The secret is shown only in this response.

schema.title: Response List Agents Api Agents Get

post.description:
Archive lost/gone identities older than N days, in a bounded batch.
With no body `older_than_days` and no `ARGUS_AGENT_ARCHIVE_AFTER_DAYS`,
answers 409 `agent_archive_disabled`. Non-lost/gone states are refused with
422 `state_not_archivable` before anything changes.
Mint a one-time token an agent redeems at registration.

get.description: Lost/gone aggregates by pool and age, claim holders, and the lost spike.
Long-poll for the next queued message, human or system (claim_task pattern).

schema.title: Response Claim Chat Api Agents Me Chat Get

get.description: Bounded history for seeding a new session after restart (3.4).

put.description: Remember the NanoClaw session id for resume (3.4).

post.description: Prove liveness and renew the listed task leases (each one independently).
Exit cleanly: the identity ends and its token is revoked.
Let the agent finish its current work, then claim nothing new.

get.description: The raw bytes. Honours `Range: bytes=…` for partial reads.

Up to `max_bytes` of a text or JSON artifact from `offset`, as UTF-8;
continue from `next_offset`. Other media types return `binary` and no bytes.

post.description:
Re-hash the stored bytes against the size and SHA-256 recorded at upload.
`ok` means intact, not acceptable.

get.description:
Decisions oldest first, in pages (max 100); open ones by default.
Workers only see decisions for tasks they have leased (and knowledge
proposals in those projects).

post.description:
Answer up to 20 decisions, each with its own explicit answer and in its own
transaction. Each item succeeds or fails on its own (`ok`, `error`).

Answer an open decision. Approvals take `approve`/`reject`, reviews
`accept`/`reject` (with `text` as notes), questions their options or text.
With a `request_id`, a retry of the same answer by the same caller returns
the stored decision with `replayed: true` instead of 409 decision_not_open.

get.description:
What answering would do, read-only and advisory (it authorizes and executes
nothing). Takes the answer's `choice`, `text` and `request_id`; reports the
verdict, transition and effects the answer path would produce, and what stored
observations say about the decision's premise. A snapshot: compare
`snapshot.decision_version` to see staleness.

Engines, executors and the local model: axes, auth methods and the three
readiness facts (installed, authenticated, validated). Read-only.

post.description:
One bounded completion on the local model, checked against `criteria`.
No tools act, so retrying or escalating duplicates no effect. An answer that
fails the criteria returns `verdict: escalate`; Argus does not start the
escalated work, the caller does.
Where should this task run? Deterministic; the decision is recorded.

A worker's channel switched its harness to follow a leased account
(codex accounts spec 3). Recorded for the audit trail; credentials never ride here.

get.description:
Event history, newest first. Page backwards with `before`. Workers only
see events for projects of tasks they have leased.

schema.title: Response List Events Api Events Get

get.description: Server-sent events. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` to resume without gaps.

Events after the cursor `after`, oldest first, waiting up to `wait_s`
seconds for one when none has happened yet (long-poll, like a claim). Without
`after`, waits for the next event from now. Keep `next_cursor` for the next
call; nothing is missed between calls. `inbox` keeps only events that add an
inbox row (MCP operations 3.3).
What this node can run right now, measured from its targets (read-only).
Pool, queue, run-time, outcome, yield and dead-session recovery over `window` hours.

The worker templates Argus supports, per node: ready, or exactly what is
missing. Read-only; nothing is created by looking.

post.description:
Create a pool from a template and request its first workers, in one
confirmed call. The pool is rebuilt server-side from the template; refusals
happen before anything is written. Success means *requested*.

get.description:
Settings, last run, per-status counts, estimated vs freed bytes, and the
latest blocked or failed directories of the workspace cleanup.
Per-directory audit rows, most recently updated first.

post.description:
Start a cleanup run now and wait up to `wait_s` for it; the summary shows
its progress. A dry run (the default) deletes nothing and works while cleanup
is disabled; `dry_run: false` needs an admin token, cleanup enabled and a
valid archive root.

get.description:
What waits on a manager, oldest first (`order=impact`: most blocked tasks
first) and grouped by project and task (`groups`): blocked, in-review and
awaiting-approval tasks with their open decision, pending tasks stuck behind a
failed or cancelled dependency (`failed_dependencies`), plus open decisions
about pools and knowledge. `state` keeps only task rows in those states;
`blocking_only` keeps rows that block at least one task (`blocks`, `impact`).
`view=actionable` adds to each row what acting on it takes (authority, effects,
impact, evidence, a suggested next action; advisory only); `forge=true` adds
bounded live PR reads to it, outside the snapshot.

schema.title: Response List Instances Api Instances Get

get.description: The container's recent output, read live from the target (not stored).

post.description:
Replace a running instance: its agents drain, it stops once none holds a
claimed task, and a new one starts in its place. By default work finishes
first; with `requeue` the claimed tasks are released now, no attempt counted.

Stop an instance now: its agents end immediately and the tasks they hold are
requeued without counting an attempt (unless `requeue` is false); its slot
frees once the provider confirms the container is gone.

schema.title: Response List Pages Api Knowledge Pages Get

post.description:
Create a page. Workers may be limited to proposing (see
ARGUS_KNOWLEDGE_WORKER_WRITES); the response says which happened.
Confirm the page is still right; resets its freshness.

schema.title: Response List Revisions Api Knowledge Pages  Page Id  Revisions Get

post.description:
Publish an edit. `base_revision_id` must be the page's current revision,
otherwise `409 knowledge_conflict`: re-read the page and apply the change again.

get.description: Proposals are resolved by answering their `knowledge` decision.

schema.title: Response List Proposals Api Knowledge Proposals Get

get.description:
Full-text search over active pages (all words must match; if nothing does,
any word may). Stale pages rank after fresh ones.

schema.title: Response Search Api Knowledge Search Get

get.description: Prometheus text format; needs an admin token (`authorization` in the scrape config).

delete.description: Remove the file so the repository defaults apply again.

get.description:
The effective policy, its origin and revision. Availability of a model at
the provider is not checked.

put.description: Validate and save the file policy, all or nothing.

get.description: Whether a fresh install has an account, a worker pool and the orchestrator.
Fleet-wide totals per state for the Home view (orchestrator or admin).
Every pool; `env` shows its keys with redacted values.

schema.title: Response List Pools Api Pools Get

delete.description:
Delete a pool definition (admin only). `confirm_name` must equal the
current name; `409 system_pool` for the internal orchestrator;
`409 pool_in_use` while any instance is not terminated. Terminated instance
rows for the pool are removed with it.

get.description: A pool; `env` values are redacted unless an admin asks for `reveal_env`.

patch.description:
Change some of a pool's options (admin only), keeping the rest. Requires
the `version` you read as `expected_version` (409 stale_version otherwise).
Name, target and runtime cannot change. `env` merges; null removes a key.

put.description:
Create or replace a pool definition, including its replica cap (admin only).
The reconciler converges instances to it within seconds. This replaces `env`
whole; PATCH changes single variables without resending the others.

get.description:
The pool, its live instances and agents, and per instance what is proven
about what runs there: each fact says its source (configured, requested,
started, validated) or `unknown`.

post.description:
Request one more worker from the pool. Refused (nothing changes) when the
node cannot start it now. Success means *requested*: the reconciler starts
the instance next pass; follow it in `/instances`.

Set desired replicas. Orchestrators may scale up to `max_replicas`; asking
for more opens a decision for a human (`decision_id`) instead of failing.

schema.title: Response List Projects Api Projects Get
Response List Routines Api Projects  Slug  Routines Get

delete.description: Remove the routine; its run tasks stay.

put.description: Create or replace. `findings: auto`, or changing an `auto` routine, is admin only.
Declare the project's runtime (admin only; versioned by the event log).

post.description: Retry the failed builds of the project's current recipe.

get.description: Effective values for a project, with `source` per key.

delete.description: Remove the project override so the global/default value is inherited.

get.description:
The stored project override alone (null value means inherit). Used by the
Settings tab when editing a partial `models` override.

schema.title: Response Get Project Override Api Projects  Slug  Settings  Key  Override Get

get.description: The routine, its next three slots and its most recent run tasks.

post.description:
Run it now, even while disabled or paused. If its previous run is still
open, nothing is created: `skipped: previous_running` (a `routine.skipped`).

get.description: The approved components and their pins: all a project may declare.

schema.title: Response Catalog Api Runtime Catalog Get

post.description:
The worker could not prepare its environment: hold the claimed task, durably
and without spending an attempt (`runtime_failed`, with `error`).

The claiming worker asks for its task project's image before any model
work. Anything but `ready` has already held the task (no attempt spent).

get.description: Selected versus actually used image of each attempt of the task.

schema.title: Response Task Runtime Api Runtime Tasks  Task Id  Get

get.description: Global values with `source` per key (env | global | default).
Every known setting key, its schema, default, scopes and description.

schema.title: Response Get Registry Api Settings Registry Get

delete.description: Remove the global row (or the model-policy file) so the default applies.

get.description: Readiness plus the numbers /metrics reports, as JSON for the dashboard.
Open drafts, oldest first; at most 200 exist, so the list is whole.

post.description:
Save a task definition that nothing can claim until it is published. Field
rules are the task's; title, spec, acceptance and project may wait for publish.

Validate drafts and create their tasks in one transaction. `atomic` (the
default) publishes all or none; `partial` publishes each valid draft and reports
the others. In-batch `depends_on_drafts` become the new task ids. A repeat with
the same `idempotency_key` and request returns the stored answer.

patch.description:
Patch an open draft: omitted fields stay, `null` resets one. A stale
`expected_version` is 409 `stale_version`; a published draft 409
`draft_published`.

schema.title: Response List Kinds Api Task Kinds Get

put.description:
Create or replace a kind. Existing tasks keep the values they were created
with; schemas apply to new tasks and to results submitted from now on.

get.description:
Tasks newest first, in pages (max 100). `assignee` is the agent holding a
task now (claimed tasks only). `ids` (comma-separated, max 50) is a batch read
instead: no other filter, no paging, unknown ids in `missing`. Archived tasks
are left out unless `archived=true`, which lists only those. Workers only see
tasks they have leased. Optional `q` is literal substring search over title
and spec (task discovery).

post.description:
Orchestrators and admins create any task; workers only subtasks of a task
they hold. Past the per-agent hourly limit, an agent's new tasks wait for
human approval (a `policy` decision) instead of being refused.

Archive terminal tasks by state, project and age, answering how many.
`dry_run` counts without writing, for a confirmation. Non-terminal states
are refused (422 `state_not_archivable`) before anything changes.
Claim a ready task, long-polling up to `wait_s` seconds for one.

204.description: No matching task became ready within wait_s

patch.description:
Edit a task's title, spec, acceptance, priority, required capabilities,
knowledge pins or dependencies (orchestrator or admin). `changes` is a partial
patch: omitted fields stay, `null` clears. Which fields a state accepts is
`editable_fields` on the task. Stale `expected_version` is 409 `stale_version`,
a field the state does not allow 409 `task_not_editable`, an immutable or unknown
field 422 `immutable_field`; a refused edit writes nothing.

post.description:
Archive a `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled` task; repeating it changes
nothing. Any other state answers 409 `task_not_terminal` and changes nothing.

get.description:
A task's artifacts (metadata only), by attempt then name; `in_result` says
whether the task's result lists one.

schema.title: Response List Artifacts Api Tasks  Task Id  Artifacts Get

post.description:
Upload the raw request body as an artifact of the attempt you hold.

List the returned id in `result.artifacts` when completing the task. `role`
says what it is for (report, delegate_report, …); it is never inferred.

Ask a question about the task you hold. The task is blocked until it is
answered; the answer is added to the task spec under "Clarifications" and
the task returns to ready.

Attach the raw request body to a task as evidence (orchestrator or admin).

Needs no lease and does not count against any agent quota. Attachments have
`source: attachment`, are immutable, and are readable by orchestrators and
admins only, unless `worker_readable` shares them with every worker holding a
lease grant on the task (then they are the task's inputs). `expected_size` and
`expected_sha256` are checked against the received bytes before anything is
stored: a difference is 422 `integrity_mismatch` and leaves no attachment.

get.description: The definition each attempt was handed at claim, oldest first.

schema.title: Response List Attempts Api Tasks  Task Id  Attempts Get

post.description:
The worker's checkpoint follow-up for an attempt whose claim has ended. Only
the agent that held the attempt may report it, and only for that attempt (409
`not_attempt_holder`, `claim_open`, `checkpoint_closed`).

get.description:
The diff snapshot of an attempt (default: the current one); 404 `no_changes`
when it has none. Workers only read tasks they have leased.

put.description:
Replace the diff snapshot of the attempt you hold (agent token), computed in
the container against the workspace's merge base. At most 384 KiB, 500 files and
a 256 KiB patch (longer is cut), one snapshot per 5 s. Secrets are redacted
before storing; the summary is published as a `task.changes` event. Fenced like
the live log: a stale attempt is 409 `stale_attempt`.

get.description:
The continuation contract: phase, known artifacts with provenance, preserved
WIP, last interruption, checklist with evidence, effective decisions and what
Argus does not know (`gaps`). Derived from stored facts; unknown is not absent.

patch.description:
Settle continuation facts (orchestrator or admin): phase, artifacts, WIP,
checklist items and evidence, environment status, retire decisions. Written with
orchestrator provenance; stale `expected_revision` is 409 `stale_continuation`.

get.description:
The state of the task's pull request as the forge shows it (open | merged |
closed | unknown), when the task names one unambiguously, else null. Read-only:
a merge flags the task for review and never closes or accepts it.

schema.title: Response Get Delivery Api Tasks  Task Id  Delivery Get

put.description:
Replace the dependencies of a task that is still waiting (pending,
awaiting_approval or ready). A ready task with an unfinished new dependency
goes back to pending; a pending one whose dependencies all succeeded becomes
ready. Refuses cycles (422 dependency_cycle) and stale versions (409).

post.description:
Fail the attempt. A `provider_failure` that is a known quota notice of the
agent's engine account is not a failure: the account is exhausted, the task
returns to ready (or waits as `awaiting_quota`) and `failures` is unchanged.

get.description:
A task's inputs: attachments shared with workers, with the size and SHA-256
Argus computed, provenance, and the latest receipt per attempt and state.
Managers also get `unshared_attachments`, a count of attachments not shared.

post.description:
Record that the attempt you hold materialized, verified, consumed or failed
an input. Fenced like progress; `sha256` and `size`, when given, must be the
artifact's (422 `integrity_mismatch`). An identical latest receipt is not
written again.

get.description:
Log lines of an attempt (default: the current one), oldest first. With
`after` (a `seq`), the lines after it; without, the newest `limit` lines.
Workers only read tasks they have leased.

post.description:
Append output lines to the live log of the attempt you hold (agent token).
Up to 200 lines of 2000 characters (longer ones are cut) and 64 KiB per batch,
one batch per second per source. Secrets are redacted before storing; the
batch is published as a `task.log` event and stored in a ring of 2000 lines
per attempt. Fenced like progress: a stale attempt is 409 `stale_attempt`.

get.description:
Every execution (both layers, all attempts, oldest first) with its evidence,
and the selection/switch timeline. Cards use the compact `models` summary.

post.description:
Report the model executions and routing decisions of the attempt the caller
holds (same lease fence as progress). Idempotent per `key`: a re-sent record
completes the stored one and never overwrites it (409 on a contradiction).

The holder's runtime reports live observations (artifact state, environment
readiness, preserved WIP) made outside any transaction. Idempotent; fenced by
the attempt like every worker write.
Post a progress note (at most one per 10 s). Also renews the lease.

Record what the channel did with the offered session (`resumed`, or a fresh
`fallback` with the reason). `first` is true once per offered session: send the
one operator message only then.

schema.title: Response Take Quota Resume Api Tasks  Task Id  Quota Resume Post

post.description:
Take a claimed task back from its holder and requeue it without counting a
failed attempt (orchestrator or admin). 409 `task_not_claimed` in any other
state, 409 `stale_attempt` when `attempt` is not the current one. The holder's
next write for that attempt gets 409 and its heartbeat rejects the pair.

get.description:
Read-only resumability preflight: attempt/lease state, WIP class, and whether
shared attachments are currently available (size and SHA-256 re-read). Recorded
metadata and historical receipts do not prove current availability. Grants
nothing; never mutates. Optional `expected_attempt` / `expected_version` make a
mismatch `stale` instead of describing a newer state.

post.description: Return a `failed` task to `ready` with a fresh window of attempts (409 otherwise).

get.description: Steers for one attempt (the current one, when `attempt` is omitted), oldest first.

post.description:
Send an instruction to the attempt in flight. The assignee must report
the `steer` feature. If the attempt ends first, the message expires, or ends
`unknown` (it may have been delivered) when a heartbeat had carried it.

delete.description: Cancel a pending steer. A delivered steer cannot be taken back.

post.description: Return an archived task to listings and totals (admin). Idempotent.
